title: Managed Identity with Azure SQL
description: Use managed identities to securely connect Azure services and applications to Azure SQL without storing credentials.

data.text: A **managed identity** is an identity in Microsoft Entra ID that is automatically managed by Azure. Any Azure resource that supports managed identities — App Service, Functions, VMs, Logic Apps — can use it to authenticate to Azure SQL without storing a username or password. This removes the biggest source of credential leaks.

When you enable a managed identity on a service, Azure creates a service principal in Entra ID. You then create a contained database user mapped to that identity in Azure SQL. The service uses its managed identity to request a token from Entra ID and presents it to Azure SQL during connection.

data.title: Grant Access Before Connecting
data.text: The managed identity must be created as a user in the database before it can connect. Use CREATE USER ... FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER for each identity that needs access.

data.title: Exercise: Connect App Service with Managed Identity
data.description: Enable managed identity, create a database user, and deploy a connected app.
steps: Enable system-assigned managed identity on an App Service.
In Azure SQL, create a user mapped to the managed identity.
Grant the user read and write permissions on a table.
Update your app to use DefaultAzureCredential with ActiveDirectoryManagedIdentity.
Deploy the app and confirm it can read and write data.
data.expectedOutcome: A deployed app that connects to Azure SQL using managed identity with no secrets in configuration.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Managed identities eliminate secrets from connection strings.
Create database users mapped to the managed identity.
System-assigned identities are per-resource; user-assigned are shareable.
DefaultAzureCredential works locally and in Azure without code changes.
data.takeaway: Managed identity is the recommended pattern for secure Azure SQL connectivity in production.
